title: Keynote Panel: From Assistants to Autonomy - Architectures Enabling Next-Gen Agents
abstract: As AI agents evolve from task-based assistants to increasingly autonomous systems, their underlying architectures must scale in intelligence, reliability, and governance. This panel explores the technical foundations enabling next-generation agents—covering multi-agent frameworks, planning and reasoning architectures, tool orchestration, memory, and human-in-the-loop controls. Industry leaders will discuss design trade-offs, real-world deployment lessons, and what it takes to move safely and effectively toward autonomous agentic systems in the enterprise.

title: Keynote Presentation: Humans + Machines - Building the Augmented Workforce and Intelligent Company
abstract: What happens when AI agents begin working together? This session introduces the concept of emergent intelligence through multi-agent systems, showing how simple rules can give rise to complex, coordinated behaviour.

title: Panel: Designing the Enterprise for Autonomous Intelligence
abstract: The next era of AI is autonomous, adaptive, and embedded across the enterprise. Unlocking that future requires more than advanced models. It requires intentional design of the systems, data, and governance that power intelligent decision-making. This keynote highlights how leading organizations are rewiring their enterprises to enable autonomous intelligence safely, responsibly, and at scale.

title: Presentation: From Stale Data to Smart Agents: The Real-Time Context Layer for Trusted Agentic AI
abstract: Agents need context. Imagine making critical business decisions relying on last month's data without the context to understand what's changed. Now layer agents on top of that scenario. Without real-time context, agents don't accelerate your business — they automate bad decisions at scale. In this session, discover what it takes to give agents a trusted data foundation: live cross-system access, a semantic layer that explains what data means, and governance applied at runtime. We will explore how streaming and historical data integration, governance and an open, hybrid data foundation work together to power agents and your business to act with confidence.

Presentation: The Real AI Apocalypse: When Token Economics Break Your Business Model
abstract: AI adoption is accelerating across every industry—but most organizations are dramatically underestimating the economic impact of running AI at scale. While early pilots focus on model accuracy and use cases, the real challenge emerges in production: token consumption, inference costs, data movement, and infrastructure inefficiencies quickly compound into unpredictable and unsustainable spend. This session explores the “hidden layer” of AI—token economics—and how it is reshaping enterprise architecture, vendor strategy, and operating models. Attendees will learn why traditional cost assumptions break down in AI workloads, how leading organizations are rethinking data and infrastructure strategies, and what practical steps can be taken today to avoid the coming AI cost crisis. The future of AI won't be limited by innovation—it will be defined by economics.

title: Lunch Break
Panel: The C-Suite Playbook for the Agentic Enterprise
abstract: As organizations race toward autonomous, AI-driven operating models, C-suite leaders face critical decisions on strategy, governance, talent, and technology. This panel brings together enterprise executives who are at the forefront of building agentic organizations, where AI agents collaborate with human teams to drive productivity, innovation, and real-time decision-making. Panelists will explore frameworks for scaling autonomous agents responsibly, aligning investments with business outcomes, navigating emerging security and compliance challenges, and reimagining workflows and culture. Attendees will gain a practical playbook for leading their organizations through the next phase of AI transformation and capturing sustainable competitive advantage.

title: Presentation: Autonomous Enterprise: Scaling Customer-Specific AI for Real Outcomes
abstract: This session explores how organizations can evolve toward an Autonomous Enterprise by embedding customer-specific AI into their core processes. It will highlight how tailored AI solutions—grounded in business context—enable smarter decision-making, continuous optimization, and faster outcomes. Through real-world perspectives, the session will demonstrate how moving from generic AI to contextual, customer-driven intelligence unlocks scalable value and transforms end-to-end operations.

abstract: How do organisations turn data and AI into measurable business outcomes? This discussion brings together product, platform, and business leaders to explore operating models that align data foundations with AI goals. Case studies will show how cross-functional teams bridge silos, balance agility with governance, and deliver ROI from AI initiatives.

Presentation: From Dashboards to AI Coworkers: How Enterprise Data Becomes Actionable
abstract: Enterprise data is everywhere, but making it useful still depends on the right people, context, and governance. The next interface is not just another dashboard — it is AI coworker agents that can collaborate with teams across systems, tables, and business history. Jorge Torres, Co-Founder and CEO of MindsDB, will explore how data teams can shepherd governed AI agents over enterprise data, helping organizations turn trusted data access into faster decisions, better workflows, and real business action.

title: Presentation: AI Building AI: How AI is accelerating Model Experimentation, and enabling the Flywheel
abstract: A meaningful shift is starting to emerge in AI. The technology is being used to build more than just products for users. It is also being used to improve the AI Infrastructure, Model Training, and optimization systems used to help build AI itself. I will elaborate to supercharge our AI iteration speed by seamlessly unifying three core pillars into one cohesive framework for experimentation at scale: – Agents for code authoring focused on distributed training. – Evaluation systems for measuring correctness, quality, and overall progress. – GPU micro scheduling for efficient use of compute.

title: Networking Break
Panel: From Data Lakes to Data Products -What's Next?
abstract: Data leaders explore how organisations are turning raw data into value-generating products and the shift in thinking required to scale. Why the data product mindset is replacing traditional data lake strategies Organisational and cultural shifts required to treat data as a product Best practices for building reusable, reliable, and scalable data products How to define ownership, SLAs, and success metrics for data products Common pitfalls and practical lessons from real-world implementations

Panel: From Hype to Impact - What's Next for Enterprise AI Agents?
abstract: Enterprise AI agents have moved beyond buzzwords and bold demos into real-world pilots and production deployments. But where is the true, measurable impact, and what will it take to scale? This panel brings together industry leaders to explore how AI agents are reshaping operations, decision-making, and customer experiences across the enterprise.

title: Presentation: The Game Electronic Arts Had to Win First: Leveling Up Their Data to Unlock AI at Scale
abstract: 62% of organizations cite poor data governance as the #1 barrier to scaling AI. Electronic Arts decided to be in the other 38%. In this fireside chat, Alation CEO & Co-Founder, Satyen Sangani, sits down with Warren Durrett, Sr. Director of Product, Data and AI, Electronic Arts, for a candid conversation about what it actually takes to build an AI-ready data foundation inside one of the world's largest game companies. Hear how Electronic Arts went from fragmented, undiscoverable data, where teams spent more time figuring out what data meant than using it, to a unified Data Marketplace powering real AI at scale. Join us to hear what broke, what worked, and what Electronic Arts learned along the way. The Conversation Will Explore – How Electronic Arts connects trusted data directly to measurable business outcomes reducing time-to-insight and accelerating decision-making – The three pillars Electronic Arts believes AI-ready data requires are: Technical Metadata, Business Context, and Institutional Knowledge and why most organizations only solve for one – How Electronic Arts' Data Marketplace enables a single governed source of truth across its game portfolio – What it really takes to deploy AI agents that analysts and executives actually trust and why that bar is higher than most organizations expect – Why Electronic Arts concluded that governance doesn't slow AI down, it's what makes AI work

title: Presentation: The AI Pipeline Starts with Storage: Architecting Scalable Data Foundations
abstract: In the race for AI supremacy, the model is the engine, but the data pipeline is the fuel line. If your pipeline is clogged by legacy cloud constraints and egress gatekeeping, your innovation stays in the garage. We're building the Neocloud architecture to keep that data moving.

title: Presentation: Finding Solid Ground in AI: A Practical Map for Smarter Decisions
abstract: This session treats AI not as magic, but as a landscape you can learn to navigate. We'll look at how different elements of it evolve over time. We'll place them on a value chain and ask a simple question: where should we be unique, and where is it safer and cheaper to rely on mature products? Finally, we'll show why building your own storage and vector infrastructure is usually a strategic distraction and how a solution such as RavenDB can occupy that central, trusted role instead.

title: Networking Break
Presentation: Getting a Handle on Master Data: How Agentic AI Is Quietly Solving the Enterprise's Oldest Problem
abstract: Master data management has been the enterprise's most expensive unsolved problem for 20 years. Traditional rule-based approaches have hit a ceiling. This session shows how agentic AI is quietly changing the economics – reframing entity resolution, stewardship, and hierarchy management as reasoning problems rather than rule problems. Drawn from two real engagements – a global food and Agri enterprise and an industrial equipment manufacturer – where agentic approaches attacked master data problems that had resisted conventional MDM programs for years. An honest look at what worked, what didn't, and what's still hard.

title: Panel: Analytics Engineering, Data Products & the Shift to Platform Thinking
abstract: Why analytics teams are moving from dashboards to data products — and how platforms enable reuse, reliability, and scale. Discussion points: Data products and ownership models Self-service analytics vs central control Enabling analytics teams without chaos

title: Presentation: Agentic AI in Motion: Building Systems That Keep Up with Your Business
abstract: AI sounds powerful in theory, but most implementations break down in fast-moving environments where speed, accuracy, and constant change define success. Static dashboards and delayed insights cannot keep up with real operational demands. In this session, JBS Dev focuses on the practical application of agentic AI in high-velocity business settings. Learn how to design systems that not only interpret data but take action within live workflows, from processing documents and resolving exceptions to dynamically adjusting operations in real time. Attendees will walk away with a clear understanding of how to apply agentic AI without slowing down their organization, how to prioritize high-impact use cases, and how to build solutions that operate continuously alongside their teams. This session is about making AI useful where it matters most, in the day-to-day flow of business.

title: Lunch Break
Presentation: Ship AI-Powered Tools and Analytics Without Sacrificing Governance: How Platform-Level Defaults Change Everything
abstract: Teams are under pressure to move fast with AI. But bolting analytics, AI agents, and governance together from separate tools creates friction, security gaps, and trust issues that slow everything down. The fix isn't better tooling. It's moving governance down a layer. When permissions are attached to your data and enforced by the platform, every app and workflow inherits enterprise-grade security by default. Not configured per app. Not dependent on whoever wrote the code knowing your security model. Just there, automatically, regardless of what tool generated the output. This session explores what that looks like in practice for teams building and shipping AI-powered analytics at enterprise scale. Key angles: – Why disconnected toolchains force a false choice between speed and compliance – What changes when security lives underneath the app instead of inside it – Real patterns for embedding human-in-the-loop oversight, RBAC, and audit trails as platform defaults

title: Presentation: The Hidden Cost of Scaling AI That Nobody Budgets For
abstract: AI projects plan for model costs, but often overlook the rapidly growing cost of data infrastructure. As AI agents scale, every query hits the warehouse, creating parallel workloads, overprovisioning, and unpredictable spend. In this session, Ido Arieli Noga, CEO & Co-Founder, Yuki, will break down where AI infrastructure costs actually come from, why they surprise even technical teams, and what organizations must change to scale AI efficiently and sustainably.

title: Presentation: From AI-Ready Data to Agentic Action: A Unified Orchestration Approach
abstract: AI agents are being deployed faster than the data infrastructure beneath them can support. Complex, siloed environments make it nearly impossible to ensure the data quality and governance AI demands. In this session, Avinash Deshpande, Workato's Field CTO for Data shows how unified data orchestration consolidates every integration pattern under one governance model, then activates trusted data through Reverse ETL, governed data products, and Enterprise MCP servers that AI agents can access and act on in real time.

title: Networking Break
Panel: Choosing the Right Data, Analytics & AI Platform Strategy
abstract: Avoiding vendor sprawl and architectural debt while keeping teams productive. Discussion points: Build vs buy vs compose Avoiding over-engineering Aligning platforms with business maturity

title: Presentation: AI and Data Upskilling for Enterprises
abstract: As organizations invest in AI, the biggest barrier to impact is skills. In this session, we explore how enterprises can build and scale AI and data capabilities across their workforce. Learn practical approaches to identifying skill gaps, aligning training to roles, and driving real business outcomes. DataCamp, a learning platform used by 18 million learners and 6,000 organizations, is helping companies upskill at scale, with some training over 40,000 employees. Learn what it takes to build AI and data skills at enterprise scale.

title: Presentation: From Data Chaos to Trusted AI: Closing the AI Pilot to Production Gap
abstract: 2026 is the year that most organizations are under pressure to move past AI pilots to production-ready agents. But success has proven elusive for many. The root cause is rarely the model – it is the data infrastructure. Without live access to governed, contextualized data, agents are left “guessing” on stale and incomplete information, and adoption stalls when business and technical teams lack confidence in their AI. This session moves past the AI hype to tackle this Pilot to Production Gap. Attendees will learn about the three critical data infrastructure requirements to deliver trustworthy AI in production, and how to help Data, AI and Business teams alike collaborate more effectively to achieve AI success more quickly. We will also show some examples of these principles in action, through customers that have achieved measurable results in production.

title: Presentation: Beyond Copilot: Architecting Agentic AI for Real Business Impact
abstract: Most organizations are experimenting with AI, but few are moving beyond copilots and isolated use cases to deliver real business outcomes. The next evolution of AI is not just generating insights. It is acting on them. In this session, JBS Dev explores how agentic AI is transforming the role of data and business intelligence by enabling autonomous decision-making within existing enterprise systems. Rather than replacing your stack, this approach layers AI directly into your BI ecosystem to automate workflows, orchestrate processes, and drive measurable results. Attendees will learn: What agentic AI actually is and how it differs from traditional GenAI tools How to integrate AI into existing data platforms without a full rebuild Real-world use cases, from invoice processing and document intelligence to inventory and workflow automation Why most AI initiatives fail to deliver ROI and how to build ones that do With practical examples and a focus on execution, this session will show how to move from passive dashboards to intelligent systems that not only inform decisions but actively make them.

title: Presentation: From Fragmented Data to Agent-Ready: How Xebia Helped an Enterprise Unify a Complex Data Estate and Build a Foundation for AI
abstract: Most organizations reach the same inflection point with AI: the models are selected, platforms are in place, and use cases are defined — but progress slows. The root cause is rarely the AI itself. It's the data. Siloed, inconsistently defined, and lacking governance, data becomes a bottleneck. While humans can work around these gaps, AI agents cannot — they act on what's available, making data quality and structure critical. In this session, we'll share how Xebia helped a large enterprise unify a complex, fragmented data landscape into a governed, scalable foundation for AI. By implementing a Medallion architecture, enforcing data contracts, and automating migration with built-in quality controls, we enabled faster, reliable data access without a full re-architecture. You'll learn the key architectural decisions, delivery approach, and how combining AI agents with expert engineering accelerated a transformation that typically takes 12–24 months.

title: Presentation: From Demos to Durable ROI
abstract: Enterprise AI has matured to the point where adoption is a no-brainer — but most organizations are still stuck between impressive demos and durable production value. The real bottlenecks have moved downstream into workflows, compliance, observability, and the decision layer. This opening session offers a practitioner's playbook for enterprise AI adoption, organized around the three layers where AI actually shows up — personal productivity, SDLC automation, and use-case automation — and the three disciplines that separate pilot purgatory from production-grade ROI: evaluation infrastructure, cost governance, and outcome metrics. Lagan walks through what's working, where adoption stalls, and how enterprise advantage comes from operational discipline — not flashy demos.

title: Presentation: Beyond the Business Case – Building a Culture of Scalable AI​
abstract: Why are some AI initiatives repeatable while others stall? This closing session explores the organisational enablers of AI at scale, including cross-functional alignment, agile data governance, and internal education strategies. Walk away with a framework for embedding AI maturity across the enterprise.

abstract: Transparency is no longer a ‘nice to have'-it's a strategic differentiator. Learn how leaders in finance, healthcare, and logistics are using explainability and communication to earn trust from users, partners, and regulators. Key Discussion Points: – What transparency looks like in real-world enterprise settings – How to communicate model behaviour across internal and external stakeholders – Examples of organisations using openness to win customer and investor confidence

title: Presentation: From Insight to Action: Closing the Last Mile of AI
abstract: Why generating insights isn't enough, and how to embed AI into workflows so decisions actually get executed at scale.

title: Presentation: Under the Hood of The World's Most Advanced AI Data Agent
abstract: Go under the hood of what it takes to build an AI agent that can actually do real-world data analysis. Hex shares lessons learned from developing an analytics agent that works across technical and non-technical interfaces. You'll learn why common “data science agent” benchmarks often overstate real performance, and why analytics is harder than coding: questions are ambiguous, follow-ups branch endlessly, and results require judgment. We'll break down the core challenges that cause inaccuracies and the practical system design choices that can make agents reliable in production. The session closes with a candid view on evaluation and governance for analytics agents, including why there's no unit test for analytical truth—and why human-in-the-loop feedback and compounding organizational context are essential for trustworthy AI in data teams.

title: Networking Break
Panel: Business Readiness at Scale – Building Cross-Functional AI Governance
abstract: As AI regulation accelerates, large organisations must go beyond checklists to build scalable, cross-functional governance. This session explores how leading companies are aligning legal, risk, and technical teams to ensure compliance, oversight, and responsible innovation across the AI lifecycle. Key updates on the EU AI Act and anticipated U.S. regulatory shifts How multinationals are adapting governance structures to stay compliant Building alignment between legal, risk, compliance, and technical teams Creating scalable frameworks for AI oversight and auditability Best practices for embedding responsible AI into product development lifecycles Balancing innovation with control in large-scale AI programmes

title: Presentation: The Enterprise Intelligence Stack: How AI Agents Turn Data into Decision Engines
abstract: Eighty-three percent of enterprises are experimenting with AI agents. Seventeen percent are getting results. The gap isn't the model, it's everything beneath it. This session makes the case that AI agents fail at the data layer, not the reasoning layer. When an agent doesn't know what your data means, who's allowed to use it, or how to interpret “churn” the same way Finance and Sales do, it produces answers your business can't trust and your teams stop asking. We'll walk through the Enterprise Intelligence Stack: a five-layer architecture that gives AI agents the context, governance, and speed they need to move from question to decision in seconds, not days. From federated query to semantic context to agentic control planes, you'll leave with a concrete framework for closing the gap between AI experimentation and AI that actually runs your business. Takeaways: How to architect a data layer that AI agents can trust. Why context is the new moat. What governance looks like in an agentic world.

title: Lunch Break
Presentation: Deploying AI Governance Platforms Across the Enterprise
Presentation: Ship Agents at Developer Speed. Without Asking Permission
abstract: Enterprises are racing to deploy AI agents — but authentication alone isn't enough. Agents that are fully credentialed can still drift, over-reach, and cause damage. Authentication answered “who.” Nobody answered “what.” This session introduces Agent Personas — where the agent's job description becomes the guardrail. Defined at deploy time, a Persona specifies allowed tools, data scopes, and rate limits. Enforcement is automatic, with no security review queues and no trade-off between speed and oversight. Developers ship faster. Security gets full visibility. Same artifact, different rooms.

title: Presentation: The Evolution of Banking Analytics
abstract: We're at a critical juncture in banking analytics. The rise of enterprise AI forces us to rethink how we integrate data for true business insight. This isn't just about new tools; it's about a fundamental shift in data strategy. We're seeing a growing tension between keeping AI data within applications and integrating it into broader analytics platforms. This choice has profound implications for how we derive value from our AI investments adhering to reliable, transparent, and responsible guardrails. Let's explore this crossroads and understand the path forward.

title: Panel: The AI Risk Stack – From LLM Monitoring to Audit Trails
abstract: A practical discussion on how enterprises are building out their AI assurance stack—covering risk classification, third-party tooling, and internal controls for ongoing monitoring, logging, and auditing. What does a modern AI risk management toolkit look like? Buy vs build: approaches to governance and compliance tooling Embedding assurance into DevOps and model monitoring pipelines

title: Panel Discussion: GenAI for Software Development - Beyond the Hype, Into the Code
abstract: What's real vs. hype: Where GenAI is already delivering value in dev workflows, and where it still falls short Velocity vs. quality: Does GenAI speed up coding without introducing new risks? Integration into the toolchain: How devs are embedding GenAI into IDEs, CI/CD, testing, and code review Shaping engineering culture: How pair programming with AI is changing team collaboration and onboarding Risk and control: Versioning, reproducibility, hallucinations — what engineers need to watch for What's next: Multi-agent dev environments, AI debugging, and the future of human-in-the-loop coding

title: Presentation: The Intelligent PDLC: Engineering Trust Into AI-Assisted Product Delivery
abstract: AI is rapidly reshaping how products are planned, built, and delivered but most enterprises are discovering that speed without trust is a liability. This session moves past models and copilots to address the harder question: how do you embed AI into the Product Development Lifecycle when data is messy, ownership is unclear, and every decision must be defensible? Drawing from real implementation patterns, we'll explore how to design AI workflows that produce evidence-backed outputs, build in evaluation and explainability from day one, structure inputs for better decisions at scale, and create human-in-the-loop controls that leaders can actually audit. You'll leave with a practical blueprint for an Intelligent PDLC, one that accelerates delivery without surrendering control.

title: Presentation: AI Agents You Can Actually Trust: Platform Best Practices for Safe AI
abstract: Your AI agent works in testing. In production, it makes unpredictable calls and breaks things. Three platform practices make agents safe: isolation, tracing, and governance. This session will show how to add them, and why infrastructure, not just prompting, is how you control AI at scale.

title: Networking Break
Presentation: AI-Powered Commerce at Scale: Generative Experiences, Autonomous Agents, Fulfillment Intelligence, and Trusted Ecosystems for the Next Retail Era
abstract: Commerce is entering an AI-native era, where intelligence is embedded across the entire commerce lifecycle—from seller onboarding to post-purchase engagement. This talk presents a full-stack blueprint for how generative AI, autonomous agents, fulfillment intelligence, and trust infrastructure are transforming modern e-commerce platforms. I'll explore how generative AI enables sellers to create rich listings from images or voice input, while real-time personalization engines and multimodal interfaces deliver seamless buyer experiences. Autonomous agents optimize inventory, pricing, and logistics. In fulfillment, AI improves routing, ETA accuracy, and delivery transparency. I'll also cover AI-driven trust systems that detect fraud, moderate content, and support compliance with global regulations like the EU Digital Services Act (DSA) and General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR). This session offers both technical depth and strategic insights for building scalable, intelligent commerce ecosystems that serve sellers, empower buyers, and sustain platform trust.

abstract: Join industry leaders for a dynamic panel discussion on how organisations are scaling innovation by harnessing the power of Generative AI, modern cloud platforms, and data-driven development. Panellists will share real-world insights, challenges, and success stories on building AI-enabled solutions, optimising cloud infrastructure, and leveraging data as a strategic asset. Learn how to navigate the evolving tech landscape and drive impactful innovation at scale.

title: Presentation: Your AI Doesn't Know What It's Talking About
abstract: Your AI agents are making decisions right now — on customer records, vendor relationships, and risk signals. But do they actually know who they're acting on? Most agentic AI pipelines are built without a resolved entity layer. They query whatever data they find — duplicated, fragmented, unverified — and act on it at scale. The result isn't a data quality problem. It's an identity problem — and it compounds with every automated action. In this session, we break down the identity gap hiding inside enterprise AI stacks and how Agentic Entity Resolution closes it. Learn real failure modes and three questions you can ask your team this week.

title: Presentation: Engineering AI Platforms for Enterprise Velocity
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, the real competitive advantage lies in platform thinking. In this session, Kapil Poreddy discusses how modern AI platforms empower developers to build, deploy, and iterate faster while maintaining governance and reliability at scale. Drawing from experience at Walmart Global Tech, this presentation covers reusable AI infrastructure, internal developer platforms, LLM integration strategies, observability for AI workloads, and balancing innovation with enterprise controls. Attendees will gain actionable insights on building AI ecosystems that enable teams – not just models – to scale.

title: Presentation: Physical AI for Industrial Maintenance and World‑Model‑Driven Decision Intelligence
abstract: Industrial assets don't fail in isolation: operating regimes shift, components influence one another, and data is often sparse or incomplete. This talk will introduce our Physical‑AI approach that combines an asset‑agnostic simulation twin, LLM agents, and a learned world model to deliver prescriptive maintenance at scale. The twin lets us generate thousands of trajectories to learn state‑transition dynamics and uncertainty and train a world model that can be used for what‑if analysis, counterfactual diagnostics, and policy optimization across reliability, safety, and cost. LLMs accelerate configuration and explainability, extracting parameters from manuals and work orders, and translating engineer intent into experiments while the world model does the reasoning: forecasting futures, testing interventions, and quantifying trade‑offs. We'll explore how this Physical‑AI framework is being developed and refined, and outline the emerging pathways toward enterprise integration—including the research directions, design choices, and practical considerations shaping its evolution.

title: Networking Break
Presentation: Accelerating Autonomous Mobility with NVIDIA DRIVE
abstract: Exploring how NVIDIA DRIVE enables autonomous vehicle development at scale through advanced AI models, high-performance compute, and simulation. This session will cover perception, decision-making, and continuous learning pipelines that power safe, efficient automated driving systems and fleet-level optimisation.

title: Presentation: Governing and Adopting Physical AI with Centralized Data and Identity in Multi-Cloud and Edge Environments
abstract: This session explores the challenges associated with deploying humanoid and physical AI systems at scale, particularly in edge and multi-cloud environments. Unlike traditional systems, such deployments involve complex combinations of local policies, multiple AI models, task workflows ranging from simple to highly sophisticated, and a diverse set of embedded devices. All of these elements must be effectively managed and governed to enable reliable production use. We will examine how these challenges can be addressed through the development of centralized data and identity frameworks. Using Azure and Data Factory as practical examples, we will demonstrate how organizations can create unified data and identity services that operate consistently across environments; these approaches are equally applicable to other hyperscale cloud platforms. The session will conclude with forward-looking proposals, including the concept of a Universal Identity Broker and the need for cross-cloud robotic protocols to support scalable, secure, and interoperable physical AI ecosystems.

title: Presentation: Scaling Physical AI with WFMs and VLA Models
abstract: The path to general-purpose robotics – Physical AI – has long been obstructed by the “Data Wall.” Traditional imitation learning requires thousands of hours of human demonstrations, making it nearly impossible to scale robot skills across diverse environments and complex tasks. This talk explores a new paradigm in robotic training: leveraging World Foundation Models (WFMs) to generate massive-scale synthetic trajectory data. We will examine the end-to-end pipeline for scaling Physical AI, beginning with the use of WFMs to “imagine” and simulate realistic future world states. We will discuss how these high-fidelity synthetic scenarios are converted into actionable data to train Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, enabling robots to understand and execute natural language instructions in unseen settings. Finally, we will cover the critical role of policy evaluation and the “real-to-real” workflow, demonstrating how these technologies collectively reduce development timelines from months to hours while significantly increasing the generalization of robotic agents.

abstract: The GenAI revolution is moving at a speed that has left even the most seasoned security leaders feeling behind. In this session, we move past the marketing hype to discuss the reality of how large enterprises are actually deploying AI. Often, this happens without the guardrails that leadership assumes are in place. We will map out the breakneck timeline of AI evolution over the past few years and explore the industry struggle summarized in the philosophy: “I don't know AI, and it is not my fault.” Learn how to bridge the gap between innovation and security using FortiAIGate. This solution provides the visibility and governance required to say “yes” to AI without compromising the enterprise.

abstract: Enterprises are racing ahead with AI adoption—often faster than security safeguards. This panel unpacks the risks and strategies to mitigate them. Jailbreaking and bypassing guardrails Preventing sensitive data leakage Sector-specific regulation (finance, healthcare)

abstract: As AI, robotics, and multi-cloud ecosystems redefine industry, cybersecurity must evolve from static defense to adaptive resilience. This session explores how AI-driven Zero Trust architectures enable organizations to innovate securely and at scale — transforming security from a control function into the foundation of speed, trust, and continuous innovation.

title: Presentation: Identity and Zero Trust for every organization - How to be prepared for an increasingly AI-driven world
abstract: As organisations accelerate AI adoption across cloud and distributed environments, identity has quietly become the most exploited attack surface – and the most underprepared. This session explores how organisations of all sizes are practically addressing this shift: deploying phishing-resistant authentication, applying Zero Trust principles without enterprise budgets, and strengthening data controls across distributed teams. Real-world approaches, measurable outcomes, and a blueprint for building resilience that scales with the business.

title: Presentation: Cybersecurity Compliance & Regulation - Transforming Risk Management Challenges into Advantages
abstract: Cyber leaders face a patchwork of frameworks – NIST, CAF, ISO, DORA, FCA rules – all demanding attention. This session cuts through the noise, showing how global organisations are streamlining compliance, avoiding duplication, and even turning regulatory pressure into a competitive advantage.

title: Presentation: How to Deliver Securely without Sacrificing Speed
abstract: Cybersecurity and speed are often framed as competing priorities, but that tradeoff is a myth. As software delivery accelerates and the traditional perimeter disappears, organizations must rethink how security is built into the development lifecycle. This talk explores how DevSecOps reframes security not as a gate, but as an enabler, one that allows teams to move faster and more safely. Drawing on real-world experience, we'll examine how modern threat landscapes, cloud-native architectures, and continuous delivery demand a new approach: embedding security into culture, workflows, and toolchains from the start. Attendees will walk away with a practical understanding of how to transform security into a competitive advantage, using “guardrails, not gates”, and how to deliver secure products at the speed the business demands. Understand why “security vs. speed” is a false tradeoff, and how to achieve both Learn how the evolving threat landscape and loss of the traditional perimeter require a DevSecOps approach Explore the core principles of DevSecOps, including culture, collaboration, and shared responsibility Gain a practical view of the DevSecOps toolchain and how to embed security across the pipeline Discover how to create “paved roads and guardrails” that enable teams to move quickly while staying secure

title: Networking Break
Presentation: Ransomware, Shadow AI, and the Race for Your Data
abstract: Data is now the primary target of cybercrime. With 96% of ransomware attacks involving data exfiltration, organisations face extortion, regulatory risk and reputational damage. Alongside ransomware, insider threats and Shadow AI – unsanctioned AI tools accessing corporate data – are increasing the risk of sensitive information leaving the organisation unnoticed. Once attackers gain access, their goal is simple: exfiltrate data before defences react. This session explores why data exfiltration is now central to cyber risk and how prevention-first strategies, including real-time exfiltration prevention and automated threat detection, can help stop ransomware, insider-driven breaches and AI-driven data loss. Key takeaways: • The shift from ransomware encryption to data exfiltration • The emerging risks of Shadow AI • Why endpoints remain critical vulnerability points • How prevention-first strategies reduce data exposure

title: Panel Discussion: Legacy Systems - The Silent Cyber Risk
abstract: From hospitals to banks, legacy platforms quietly prop up critical services – until they don't. Breaches too often trace back to “that old system everyone knew was a problem.” This panel confronts the elephant in the server room: how do you modernise before it's too late? Real-world stories will reveal the costs of delay versus the benefits of decisive action.

title: Presentation: After the Leak - How Invisible Watermarking Fills the Gap Traditional Security Leaves Open
abstract: Leaks don't discriminate. In 2025, every one of the world's ten largest companies and all fifteen U.S. cabinet-level departments experienced a damaging insider leak. Most had mature DLP, IRM, and SIEM deployments, but these solutions weren't designed to stop a motivated insider with access, using off-network leak methods, like photographing a screen or printed page with a personal device. Invisible forensic watermarking takes a different approach. Instead of trying to stop information from moving, it embeds a unique, imperceptible identity into every copy before it ever leaves. Workflows don't change, recipients see nothing – but when sensitive content surfaces where it shouldn't, that embedded identity connects back to the specific copy that was leaked, in minutes, with forensic evidence and chain of custody documentation. This session covers how the technology actually works: the steganographic foundations behind content-embedded watermarking, why it survives the analogue gap (photos, printouts, low-resolution reproductions), and what leak investigation looks like in practice – with live demonstrations across real-world scenarios.

title: Lunch Break
Presentation: The node_modules Iceberg - Mysteries Below the Waterline
abstract: What lurks below the tip of the iceberg? Well, if you look at it from the aspect of web and software, it is our best friend, the node_modules. Have you ever jumped into your node_modules and looked around to see what the various packages of your packages are? Chances are, no. We don't have time for that…but we should! Let's dive into the world of transitive dependencies and break down what they are. In this session, you will learn what transitive dependencies are, how to identify them, the risks they pose, and how to integrate TuxCare's ELS solution to address them.

title: Presentation: Before the CVE - Anticipating Threats in Complex Enterprise Environments
abstract: What if security prevention didn't begin when a CVE is published? As vulnerability weaponization timelines compress, waiting for disclosure can put organizations behind the curve. This session explores how predictive forecasting, historical weakness patterns, and structured threat simulation can help enterprises anticipate likely exposures before they are publicly reported, strengthening defenses proactively rather than reactively. Attackers don't wait for disclosure Weaponization timelines shrinking Historical weakness patterns repeat Exposure is heavily weighted in open-source code Predictive threat assurance includes structured vulnerability forecasting + simulation + human validation.

title: Panel Discussion: The Human Factor - Empowering the CISO and the C-Suite
abstract: Boards are demanding more from CISOs, but how can organisations balance responsibility, authority, and support? CISO–Board communications best practice Avoiding “blame culture” in the event of a breach Building executive alliances across business function

title: Networking Break
Presentation: AI A to Z - The 26 Decisions Every Enterprise Leader Must Make - and the Order That Matters
abstract: Seventy percent of enterprise AI pilots never reach production — not due to lack of ambition or investment, but because of poor foundational decisions. This session breaks down the critical choices that determine whether AI delivers real business value or becomes technical debt. Structured A to Z across key domains including architecture, data, governance, security, and ROI, it provides a practical framework for scaling AI effectively. Drawing on real-world examples from organisations such as Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Walmart, NHS England, and Klarna, this session highlights what works – and what doesn't. Attendees will leave with a clear decision-making framework to guide their own AI strategy, from initial deployment through to enterprise-wide scale.

title: Presentation: 48% of cyberattacks involve web browsers: Is it time to reimagine the security perimeter?
abstract: Modern cyberattacks are increasingly originating and executing within the browser, often spanning multiple stages of the cyber kill chain. This shift exposes a critical visibility gap, as traditional endpoint and network security controls lack insight into browser runtime behavior. To address this challenge, a Browser-Native Security stack is emerging, redefining the enterprise security boundary. In this talk, we will review the key challenges associated with modern web browsing and review emerging technologies designed to mitigate these risks. Attendees will leave with a clear understanding of the evolving threat landscape and practical insights into adopting browser-native controls to enhance their security posture.

title: Presentation: Breaking the Trust Assumption - Defending Mobile Apps in Untrusted Environments
abstract: Mobile applications are now a primary interface for commerce, identity, and customer engagement, making them a growing attack surface. As attackers shift from network-based threats to client-side manipulation, many traditional security assumptions no longer apply. This session explores how modern attacks target mobile applications through reverse engineering, tampering, cloning, and API abuse, and why securing mobile environments requires a move from implicit trust to continuous validation. It outlines a practical, defence-in-depth approach to protecting applications and backend services while maintaining performance and development efficiency.

title: Fireside Chat: My Transformation Stalled – What's Gone Wrong?
abstract: In this session, we will explore why many transformation initiatives lose momentum and struggle to deliver results. Participants will learn to identify common obstacles, from unclear objectives and resistance to change, to cultural barriers and insufficient measurement of impact. We will discuss practical strategies for diagnosing issues early, re-engaging stakeholders, and reigniting progress. Attendees will also discover actionable approaches to get stalled transformations back on track and ensure long-term success.

title: Presentation: Workflow Automation to Agentic Intelligence – End-to-End Transformation in Financial Services
abstract: This session examines the shift from traditional workflow automation to agentic intelligence in large-scale financial services. Drawing on real enterprise transformations, it shows how organizations can move from task-based automation to end-to-end, self-orchestrating operations that combine workflow, decisioning, robotics, and responsible AI. Attendees will learn practical architecture, governance, and operating models to scale automation securely and compliantly, prioritize high-value use cases, and measure business impact as they progress toward supervised autonomy.

title: Presentation: Digital Transformation That Actually Works: From Idea to Impact
abstract: Everyone is talking about digital transformation, but most initiatives stall, overcomplicate, or fail to deliver meaningful results. The problem isn't the technology. It's the disconnect between business goals and execution. In this session, JBS Dev breaks down what digital transformation actually means in practice and how to approach it in a way that drives measurable impact. Instead of focusing on tools, trends, or buzzwords, this talk centers on solving real business problems through pragmatic, outcome-driven solutions.

title: Networking Break

abstract: AI doesn't replace people — it empowers them. This presentation explores how combining human creativity with AI-driven insights is creating new ways of working, improving decision-making, and accelerating transformation outcomes. Attendees will learn practical frameworks for deploying AI to enhance, not disrupt, the workforce.

title: Presentation: Streamlining the CX Journey: Driving Value by Eliminating Support Friction
abstract: When technical deployment outpaces human readiness, organizations experience “digital friction”: low adoption, poor data integrity, and a fragmented Digital ecosystem. This session explores how to shift from static training to adaptive, context-aware learning, embedded directly in the digital applications, reducing cognitive load and accelerating time to proficiency.

title: Lunch Break
Panel: Measuring Success: ROI of AI and Automation in Business Transformation
abstract: In this session, we will explore how organisations can measure the impact of AI and automation initiatives to demonstrate real business value. Participants will learn practical approaches to quantify ROI, track performance, and balance short-term gains with long-term transformation goals. We will discuss the importance of linking technology outcomes to business objectives, setting clear metrics, and communicating results effectively to stakeholders. Attendees will also discover tools and strategies to optimise AI and automation investments, maximise efficiency, and ensure sustainable transformation success.

title: Presentation: The Exit Strategy from Microsoft and Google
abstract: In this session, attendees will explore practical approaches to reducing dependency on major cloud providers such as Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. We will examine the key challenges organizations face when addressing vendor lock-in including pricing volatility, data sovereignty concerns, regulatory exposure such as the US CLOUD Act, and the operational complexities of data migration. Drawing on real-world examples, the session will highlight how organizations are rethinking their collaboration strategies to regain control over their data, improve flexibility, and build more resilient and sovereign digital environments.

title: Fireside Chat: How AT&T Turned Copilot into Measurable Business Impact
abstract: What does enterprise AI adoption look like when it actually works? AT&T scaled Microsoft 365 Copilot to a large and growing user base in a matter of weeks — achieving a remarkable adoption rate and significant monthly business value. In this Q&A, Prosci's Romona Brown sits down with leaders from AT&T and Microsoft to unpack the people-first strategy behind the results, and how this momentum continues as adoption expands and business impact deepens. What you'll hear: How AT&T overcame change fatigue, governance complexity, and a competing internal AI platform, and why structured change management was the difference between a rollout and a result. What you'll take away: Concrete, proven practices for driving measurable AI adoption ROI in your own organization, straight from the teams who delivered it.

title: Networking Break
Panel: Unifying Teams for Successful Digital Transformation: Strategies for Engagement and Collaboration
abstract: In this dynamic session, we will explore effective strategies for rallying teams around digital transformation initiatives. Participants will learn how to foster a culture of collaboration and engagement that drives successful outcomes. We will discuss the importance of clear communication, inclusive leadership, and shared vision in aligning diverse teams toward common goals. Attendees will also discover practical tools and techniques to overcome resistance to change, encourage cross-functional cooperation, and empower team members at all levels.

title: Presentation: Igniting Enterprise‑Level Digital Transformation - From Rethinking the Business to Applying AI at Scale
abstract: This session will explore how a “rethink‑first, then apply AI” approach guided Constellation's multi‑year digital transformation and expanded into a portfolio of strategic, enterprise‑wide impact. Digital transformation is often misunderstood as a technology upgrade—but real, enterprise‑level change begins by rethinking how people work, how value is created, and how operating models must evolve before AI is ever applied. This keynote unveils how Constellation turned that mindset into action, transforming an exploratory digital effort into a modernized, AI‑enabled operating model that is now delivering measurable value.

abstract: Generative AI is reshaping industries from finance and healthcare to manufacturing and retail. In this panel, leaders from multiple sectors will share real-world examples of how they are applying GenAI to solve industry-specific challenges, enhance innovation, and deliver measurable business outcomes. The discussion will explore best practices for implementation, strategies for overcoming adoption hurdles, and how to align AI initiatives with broader transformation goals. Attendees will gain cross-industry insights into unlocking opportunities and accelerating digital transformation through generative AI.

title: Presentation: From Innovation to Impact: Making Digital Transformation Earn Its ROI
abstract: Digital transformation has become table stakes – but returns remain uneven. In this session, Dr Erin Boyd shares how AES reframed digital not as a technology agenda, but as a decision system grounded in economic discipline. Rather than focusing on tools or trends, the session examines how leaders make funding, prioritization, and adoption decisions – and why those choices determine whether digital investments show up in the P&L.

title: Presentation: The AI Agent Playbook for People Building on Top of APIs, Not Hype
abstract: AI agents are generating a lot of noise, but enterprise teams still need to work with the systems they already run: APIs, integrations, events, workflows, and governance models built over years. This session looks at what an actual AI agent playbook looks like for organizations building on top of that foundation, not starting from scratch. We'll explore how agents connect to enterprise capabilities, where MCP and tool-based access fit, and why control, observability, and policy matter as much as intelligence. Attendees will leave with a clearer way to think about where agents add value, where they add risk, and how to tell the difference.

title: Networking Break
Presentation: From Change Fatigue to Change Readiness: Designing Digital Transformation Around the People Behind the Product
abstract: Digital transformation often creates an unintended burden: new tools, workflows, and expectations layered onto already complex product organizations. The result is change fatigue, weak adoption, and limited business impact—especially when teams still operate in silos. In this fast-paced 10-minute session, we'll explore how a human-centered, data-centric approach can connect product information from inception to end of life, making transformation easier to adopt and sustain. By reducing reliance on disconnected documents and fragmented systems, organizations can improve collaboration, strengthen trust in decisions, and deliver better outcomes, achieving short-term wins while building a resilient foundation for long-term innovation.

title: Presentation: When 'Later' Costs $1.2 Billion
abstract: Every organization carries technical debt. Few can say what it costs. This session introduces Cost of Delay, a practical framework for turning tech debt from an IT grievance into a business decision, scored, ranked, and tied to real dollars lost per month of inaction.

title: Presentation: Transforming the DMV - How a Legacy Agency Scaled Digital Services and AI State-wide
abstract: This session will share the ongoing journey of transforming one of largest customer facing Government agencies in the nation into a “digital first” service delivery organization via rapid change accelerators involving Intelligent Automation, Artificial Intelligence, Digital Credentials, Decision-making Intelligence and Process Leaning.

From Silicon Valley to City Hall: Driving Public Innovation in San José
abstract: San José stands at the forefront of municipal innovation, leveraging its position in the heart of Silicon Valley to pilot new approaches to public service delivery, digital infrastructure, and inclusive economic growth. This session will explore how the City is advancing data-driven governance, fostering public-private partnerships, and investing in emerging technologies such as AI, smart infrastructure, and broadband expansion. Stephen will highlight lessons learned from deploying innovation at scale, balancing speed with equity, and experimentation with accountability, while ensuring that technological progress translates into tangible benefits for all residents.

title: Presentation: From Data to Dollars: Dow's AI Transformation
abstract: AI is no longer a technology experiment, it's a business transformation engine. In this session, Chris Bruman explores how organizations can unlock real value from AI by treating data as a strategic asset, not a byproduct. Drawing on enterprise-scale experience, Chris will outline five critical pillars: building trusted data foundations, aligning AI to business outcomes, activating high‑impact use cases across operations and customer experience, and governing AI responsibly at scale. Attendees will leave with practical insights on how to move beyond pilots, earn executive confidence, and use AI to drive measurable growth, productivity, and competitive advantage.

title: Fireside Chat: From Quick Wins to Lasting Impact: Making Decisions That Strengthen Long-Term Transformation
abstract: Balancing immediate results with a long-term strategy is key to successful transformation. Participants will explore how to deliver quick wins that build momentum while keeping sight of broader organisational goals. The discussion will cover aligning stakeholders, managing expectations, and maintaining focus during complex change initiatives. Attendees will also discover practical approaches to create a roadmap that balances short-term achievements with sustainable, long-term transformation success.

abstract: As organizations invest in intelligent automation, measuring tangible business value becomes critical. Industry leaders will share real-world examples, discuss challenges in tracking ROI, and offer strategies to demonstrate measurable outcomes to stakeholders. Attendees will leave with actionable insights to assess, justify, and optimize the value of their automation projects.

title: Presentation: Technical Deep Dive: Agentic Automation & Autonomous Systems – What's Next?
abstract: As automation evolves beyond scripted workflows, agentic automation and autonomous systems are redefining how machines interact, learn, and make decisions. This technical deep dive will explore the architectures, frameworks, and real-world applications driving this next wave of automation. Attendees will gain insights into how autonomous agents leverage AI, orchestration layers, and decision intelligence to operate with minimal human intervention. The session will also examine emerging use cases, integration challenges, and the path toward scalable, reliable, and secure autonomous systems in enterprise environments.

title: Presentation: Beyond RPA: A New Approach to Production-Grade Enterprise Automation
abstract: Agentic AI looks impressive in clean trial environments, but most organizations still struggle to deploy it in production. Enterprises face variability is data configurations, frequently changing web interfaces, and hurdles such as Citrix-only access. Such challenges cause hard-coded bots to constantly break and naive applications of frontier models to generate inconsistent results. In this session, David Park, CEO and Co-founder of Narada AI, will outline a new approach to production-grade agentic automation: AI agents that can plan, orchestrate, execute, validate, and self-heal across enterprise workflows. Drawing on real-world examples from customer deployments, he will show how enterprises can reduce implementation time, minimize break-fix cycles, and achieve automation outcomes that go beyond demos to deliver measurable ROI.

title: Networking Break
Presentation: Building Enterprise-Ready Robotics: Integration, Reliability & ROI
abstract: Deploying robotics at scale is more than just installing machines – it requires careful planning, integration, and alignment with business objectives. This session explores the journey from pilot projects to enterprise-wide deployments, highlighting strategies to ensure reliability, interoperability, and measurable ROI. Attendees will learn how organizations overcome technical and operational challenges, integrate robotics with existing systems, and design processes that maximize value. Through real-world examples, the session provides practical insights for leaders and technical teams seeking to transform automation experiments into sustainable, enterprise-ready solutions.

title: Presentation: AI Isn't the Advantage - Execution Is: Why AI-Powered OKRs Will Define the Next Generation of Enterprise Performance
abstract: AI is now a commodity, but most organizations still struggle with slow decisions and fragmented execution. The real advantage lies not in adopting AI, but in turning insights into coordinated, scalable action. Many AI initiatives fail due to poor alignment and execution – not technology – often amplifying inefficiencies instead of solving them. This session introduces AI-powered OKRs as a new operating model to drive organizational velocity, using real-time insights and structured goal alignment to improve visibility, speed up decisions, and connect strategy to measurable outcomes.

title: Lunch Break
Presentation: Automating large scale applications
Presentation: The New Standard for IT Operations: Action at AI Speed
abstract: As AI drives an exponential increase in signals across applications, networks, and infrastructure, IT operations have reached an inflection point. Visibility is no longer the constraint. The real challenge is acting on what matters at the speed and scale that modern environments demand. Fragmented tools, delayed coordination, and manual workflows cannot keep pace. This session explores how governed, agentic AI establishes a new operational model. By correlating signals across domains, reasoning over real-time context, and executing within clear governance guardrails, these systems move beyond insight to decisive action that helps compress time to resolution, align decisions to business impact, and enable resilient operations that scale with the complexity of AI-driven systems.

title: Networking Break
Presentation: Operationalizing AI: Governance, Visibility and Scale in Intelligent Automation with Python
abstract: While AI has accelerated the creation of automations, moving from fragmented scripts to scalable, enterprise-grade operations remains a challenge. Most organizations are running Python-based automations without real-time visibility into execution, hindering ROI and operational stability. This session explores how to transition from isolated scripts to orchestrated, high-performance intelligent automation. By leveraging BotCity Sentinel, leaders can gain a live inventory of all Python executions, ensuring every script delivers measurable value. Learn how to implement a governance-first approach that acts as a catalyst for scale, enabling innovation with full visibility, evidence-based control, and predictable operational metrics.

title: Presentation: Designing Agentic AI Systems That Work: Lessons from Real-World Deployments
abstract: Agentic AI is moving from concept to competitive advantage but making it work in the real world is no small feat. In this session, discover how to design agentic AI systems that truly deliver systems that reason, adapt, and scale responsibly. Drawing from real-world deployments across industries, we'll unpack the strategies, architectures, and lessons learned that bridge visionary ideas with enterprise-grade execution. Whether you're a business leader shaping AI strategy or an engineer building the future, this talk will show how to turn agentic intelligence into impact.

title: Presentation: Physical AI for Industrial Maintenance and World‑Model‑Driven Decision Intelligence
abstract: Industrial assets don't fail in isolation: operating regimes shift, components influence one another, and data is often sparse or incomplete. This talk will introduce our Physical‑AI approach that combines an asset‑agnostic simulation twin, LLM agents, and a learned world model to deliver prescriptive maintenance at scale. The twin lets us generate thousands of trajectories to learn state‑transition dynamics and uncertainty and train a world model that can be used for what‑if analysis, counterfactual diagnostics, and policy optimization across reliability, safety, and cost. LLMs accelerate configuration and explainability, extracting parameters from manuals and work orders, and translating engineer intent into experiments while the world model does the reasoning: forecasting futures, testing interventions, and quantifying trade‑offs. We'll explore how this Physical‑AI framework is being developed and refined, and outline the emerging pathways toward enterprise integration—including the research directions, design choices, and practical considerations shaping its evolution.

abstract: Exploring how NVIDIA DRIVE enables autonomous vehicle development at scale through advanced AI models, high-performance compute, and simulation. This session will cover perception, decision-making, and continuous learning pipelines that power safe, efficient automated driving systems and fleet-level optimisation.

title: Presentation: Scaling Physical AI with WFMs and VLA Models
abstract: The path to general-purpose robotics – Physical AI – has long been obstructed by the “Data Wall.” Traditional imitation learning requires thousands of hours of human demonstrations, making it nearly impossible to scale robot skills across diverse environments and complex tasks. This talk explores a new paradigm in robotic training: leveraging World Foundation Models (WFMs) to generate massive-scale synthetic trajectory data. We will examine the end-to-end pipeline for scaling Physical AI, beginning with the use of WFMs to “imagine” and simulate realistic future world states. We will discuss how these high-fidelity synthetic scenarios are converted into actionable data to train Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, enabling robots to understand and execute natural language instructions in unseen settings. Finally, we will cover the critical role of policy evaluation and the “real-to-real” workflow, demonstrating how these technologies collectively reduce development timelines from months to hours while significantly increasing the generalization of robotic agents.

title: Presentation: How to Take Control of the Chaos in Data Center Construction and Actually Deliver on Time
abstract: Drawing on real-world experience from hyperscale builds, Brad Barton, VP of Construction at Applied Digital, shares how to bring order to the chaos of modern data center construction. From managing aggressive timelines and navigating supply chain pressures to coordinating multiple stakeholders, this session explores what it really takes to deliver complex projects on time. Gain practical insights into leadership, planning, and execution strategies that drive certainty in an unpredictable construction landscape

title: Presentation: GRID-FREE POWER. ALWAYS ON: Independent Power for Data Centers
abstract: When surging power demand outpaces the grid, innovation becomes mission critical. Langley delivers a proven, behind-the-meter power solution providing scalable, stabilized, utility-grade power – exactly where and when it's needed. Langley's Power Solutions Division brings together three wholly owned subsidiaries, each a global leader in their field: Bergen Engines (formerly Rolls-Royce Bergen Engines) of Norway; Italian generator specialist Marelli Motori; and Germany's gold standard in power conditioning and stabilization, Piller Power Systems. Designed for speed and scale, our modular solutions can be rapidly deployed up to 500+ MW and beyond, dramatically cutting lead times. While traditional grid connections can take a decade or more, Langley's unrivalled time-to-power enables critical infrastructure to move forward – without waiting for the grid to catch up.

title: Networking Break
Fireside Chat: Powering Prosperity: Santa Clara's Data Center Strategy and Its Economic Impact
abstract: Santa Clara has emerged as a leading hub for data centers, with dozens of facilities powering cloud services, AI computing and digital infrastructure across Silicon Valley. These data centers contribute tens of millions of dollars annually to the city's general fund through utility revenues, property taxes, and use taxes, making them one of the largest non-taxpayer revenue streams for local services. The city's municipally owned utility, Silicon Valley Power, offers competitive rates and strong fiber connectivity that attract this industry, even as investments in grid upgrades and land-use planning aim to balance growth with sustainability.

title: Presentation: Data Center Procurement Tips – Best Practices to Specify, Procure, Deploy and Manage 400V/415V 3PH 60A–125A Intelligent PDUs
abstract: The specification of the rack PDU is a key design milestone for all AI deployments. This one spec locks in: Cabinet power density with consequent cooling requirements Cabinet form factor Upstream electrical distribution topology requirements Receptacle counts for planned GPU server configurations Standards for cabinet level metering, receptacle remote control, and environmental and security monitoring Point-of-use data collection for data center efficiency and other performance metrics Real-time data streams for DCIM software for proactive power management, 3phase load balancing, identification of GPU power supply anomalies avoidance of constraints that can lead to GPU thermal shutdown visibility of available resources for future deployments

title: Presentation: The Network: The Key Lever in Improving AI Factory MFU and Token Efficiency
abstract: During this presentation, Chris Summers of Aria Networks will examine the network fabric not as a passive, unintelligent conduit, but as the most significant variable in determining the performance of an AI cluster. Although the network accounts for only 10-15% of the total cluster expenditure, a marginal 1% enhancement in Model Flops Utilization (MFU) effectively offsets the entire capital investment in the network, establishing it as the most cost-effective area for optimization. Consequently, an underperforming network compromises the efficiency of the entire stack, whereas an optimized network enhances the performance of all associated components.

title: Lunch Break
Panel: Powering Growth: Overcoming Energy and Water Constraints in the Data Centre Industry
abstract: As global data demand accelerates, access to reliable, scalable energy and water resources has emerged as one of the most significant barriers to new data centre development. This panel explores how operators and developers are confronting grid capacity limits, infrastructure bottlenecks, and increasing water scarcity that together threaten deployment timelines and siting decisions. Experts will discuss strategies including diversified power sourcing, on-site generation, advanced cooling technologies, improved water stewardship, and collaborative planning with utilities and municipalities. Attendees will gain insight into how the industry can future-proof capacity growth while enhancing efficiency, resilience, and sustainability in an increasingly resource-constrained world.

title: Presentation: Engineering Cooling Systems That Perform Under Pressure
abstract: From chilled water loops to ultra‑pure water (UPW) systems, resilient water infrastructure is essential for thermal management, uptime, and sustainability in mission‑critical environments. In this presentation, we'll show how engineering teams use PIPE‑FLO to design, model, and validate water‑based systems that deliver reliable performance today—and scale for the future. Topics include: – Validate flow and pressure in complex cooling and water systems – Design for resilience, redundancy, and future expansion – Model UPW, chilled water, and process cooling networks – Select and size pumps and loops for variable operating loads – Apply predictive modeling and simulation to reduce risk and improve system durability

title: Panel: Building North America's AI Spine: High‑Density, Sustainable, and Connected Data Center Infrastructure.
abstract: North America is entering an unprecedented era of AI‑driven infrastructure growth, with demand for high‑density compute, resilient networks, and sustainable facilities reaching historic highs. This session brings together five leading Québec‑based innovators whose combined capabilities support the rapid expansion of data center capacity across the continent. This panel explores how an integrated North American ecosystem can accelerate deployment, enhance resiliency, and enable the next generation of AI and cloud services.

abstract: See how Subzero Engineering is pushing containment forward with innovations no one else offers, including new low GWP materials engineered for greener, smarter data center whitespace.

title: Panel: From Sensory to Strategy - Turning Operations Data into Business Value
abstract: As automation takes on more of the technical workload, the engineer's role is shifting from manual control to analytical oversight. This discussion explores how operational and data science skills are merging, what upskilling looks like in AI-assisted environments, and how human expertise remains critical in an era of intelligent automation.

title: Panel: From Power to Performance: Addressing Today's Data Center Challenges
abstract: Modern data centers face a complex landscape of operational, technical, and strategic challenges—from energy constraints and cooling demands to scalability, security, and cost pressures. This panel brings together industry leaders to discuss how organizations are tackling these hurdles, sharing insights, lessons learned, and best practices to optimize performance, ensure resilience, and drive long-term value.

title: Fireside Chat: Hiding in Plain Sight: Simple Healthy Buildings Strategies for Data Centers to Unlock Massive Energy Savings
abstract: As data center energy demand rises, much of the focus has been on complex solutions—but are we missing the low-hanging fruit? This session explores how simple Healthy Building interventions can deliver major benefits. Using a Virginia case study, we show how low-cost upgrades to materials and air filtration reduce energy use and costs, then scale this across 200 existing and 200 planned sites to estimate statewide energy, climate, and health impacts using Harvard's CoBE tool. We also highlight how real-time air quality monitoring supports performance verification, smarter maintenance, and resilience.

title: Networking Break
Panel: From CapEx to OpEx: Re-Engineering the Commercial Model for Modern Data Centres
abstract: Flexible contracts and usage-based pricing are transforming how operators manage risk and profitability. This presentation will explore the operational and financial benefits of consumption models, how to embed ESG metrics into pricing strategies, and methods for sharing risk and increasing transparency. Attendees will learn how modern commercial models can drive both business efficiency and customer satisfaction.

title: Presentation: How agility in IT Ops supports the AI Data Center
abstract: Agile IT Ops drives AI Data Center success by enabling rapid scaling, in-depth observability, and seamless collaboration between IT and data teams thereby shortening time-to-revenue for capex intensive AI infrastructure investments. Effective workforce management ensures the right skill alignment with AI demands, empowering teams to quickly adapt and optimize operations for continuous improvement.

title: Presentation: Energy Efficiency in Digital Infrastructure: The Opportunity Beneath the Challenge
abstract: Energy efficiency is at the heart of building truly sustainable digital infrastructure. While design plays an important role, the way a data center is operated day to day—how energy is monitored, managed, and optimized—has an even greater long-term impact. Improving energy efficiency won't solve every challenge facing data center operators, but it can address many of them—reducing environmental impact, lowering operating costs, and strengthening operational resilience. Small improvements in how facilities are measured, managed, and optimized can translate into significant savings at scale. This presentation will look at practical steps operators can take to improve their energy efficiency from lessons learned in the field.

title: Presentation: The Cost of Loss in a $Trillion Infrastructure Race
abstract: We are in the middle of the greatest infrastructure buildout in history. GPUs, racks, and modular data center systems are moving at unprecedented scale — and nearly half of all US data center projects planned for 2026 are already delayed. Capital is flowing, but timelines are not. In every gold rush, fortunes weren't lost at the source. They were lost in movement — in theft, in breakdowns, in the moments where no one was watching. Today, a single lost shipment of AI hardware can trigger export scrutiny, regulatory exposure, criminal interception, and strategic delay measured in weeks — not quarters. David Warrick explores what's really at stake when the AI hardware supply chain control breaks down across transit and on-site operations — and what AI leaders building at speed are doing differently.

title: Lunch Break
Presentation: Dark Data Centers: Robots Remaking AI Infrastructure
abstract: Imagine a dark data center—no lights, no human presence, operating in complete autonomy. Expert robots and technician robots don't just maintain equipment; they fully orchestrate AI infrastructure: training models, optimizing compute allocation, predicting capacity needs, and continuously expanding and reshaping computational power. This isn't about incremental improvement. It's about extreme efficiency and radical resource optimization—where the data center becomes the physical embodiment of AI, and robots become AI's architects and operators.

abstract: Backup generators are essential to data center reliability, but they also introduce hazardous air pollutant challenges. In this session, Rypos demonstrates how active filtration technologies reduce harmful emissions, protect sensitive infrastructure, and help data centers meet environmental requirements while maintaining full operational readiness.

title: Panel: Building the Next Generation of Data Centers: Overcoming Development and Infrastructure Challenges
abstract: As demand for digital infrastructure continues to surge, developing the next generation of data centers requires a holistic approach that balances cost, performance, and sustainability. This session will explore the key challenges shaping data center expansion — from power availability and connectivity to site strategy, scalability, and environmental impact. Attendees will gain insights into how operators, technology leaders, and developers are navigating these factors to build resilient, efficient, and future-ready facilities.
